Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Dysuria with foul-smelling urine; no identifiable precipitating trigger.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Acute onset 6 days ago; intermittent lower-mid abdominal pain (7/10); spotting of blood in urine; no change in intensity reported today.
- ENT symptoms: Patient denies or did not report throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, or neck pain/swelling. (Not discussed in visit.)
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: No prior urinary infections; first episode. No prior ED visits or injections.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergy: Clindamycin (reaction details not documented).  
  • Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg PO TID (regular).  
  • No rescue medications or auto-injector reported.
- Any relevant social context: Lives with friends; works as support worker; single-glass wine/week; non-smoker; consult conducted privately at home.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: None reported.
- Airway/breathing: No distress, stridor, or dyspnea reported.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (remote consultation).
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not stated.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression: Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis.
  Evidence: 6-day history of dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, microscopic hematuria; afebrile; no flank pain or systemic upset.
- DDx (aligned with transcript):
  1. Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis – high likelihood; classic symptom cluster; no upper-tract signs.
  2. Urethritis (STI-related) – medium likelihood; dysuria/hematuria could represent urethral inflammation; opposing evidence: denies precipitating sexual risk factors, no vaginal discharge.
  3. Urinary tract calculi – low-medium likelihood; hematuria and pain support; opposing: pain non-colicky, no flank radiation.
- No transcript–DDx conflicts noted.

Plan:
- Immediate actions: Prescription for 3-day oral antibiotic course sent electronically to patient’s nominated pharmacy (Knightsbridge); patient to commence promptly.
- Supportive measures: Increase oral fluids to 2.5–3 L/day; consider cranberry juice; OTC urinary alkalinizing sachets (details provided in notes).
- Monitoring/education: Purchase thermometer; check temperature periodically. Remain alert for red flags: rising fever (>38 °C), flank/loin or worsening lower-back pain, increasing abdominal pain, vomiting, difficulty passing urine, visible blood, or persistent/worsening symptoms after antibiotics.
- Escalation: If red flags develop or symptoms recur frequently, contact GP service or seek urgent care.
- Follow-up: No routine review required if fully recovered; return if no improvement within course or if recurrent episodes develop. Consider urinalysis/culture or STI screen at follow-up if symptoms persist.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected: No urine dipstick/culture, no vitals (temp, HR, BP), no documentation of urinary frequency/urgency, sexual history limited, no ENT-specific assessment given presenting complaint was GU-related.  
● Transcript–DDx conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio, minimal background noise; clinically complete for basic GU assessment but limited objective data.
